question: 'Natyashashtra', the earliest text dealing with performing arts (dances and music), was compiled by which sage?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Natyashastra' is an ancient Indian treatise on the performing arts, encompassing theatre, dance, and music.
 
• It was written by the sage Bharata Muni, who is regarded as the father of Indian theatrical art forms.
 
• The text is believed to have been composed between 200 BCE and 200 CE.
 
• 'Natyashastra' consists of 36 chapters with a total of 6000 shlokas (verses).
 
• It provides a detailed description of various aspects of stage performance, including music, dance, stage design, and the art of acting.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharata Muni:** He is considered one of the pioneers in the field of dramatics and performing arts in India.
 
• **Rasa Theory:** The 'Natyashastra' introduces the concept of 'Rasa,' which refers to the emotional essence or flavor that the audience experiences during a performance.
 
• **Eight Rasas:** The text identifies eight primary Rasas: Shringara (love), Hasya (laughter), Karuna (sorrow), Raudra (anger), Veera (heroism), Bhayanaka (fear), Bibhatsa (disgust), and Adbhuta (wonder).
 
• **Dance Forms:** The 'Natyashastra' outlines the classical dance forms of Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kuchipudi, Odissi, and others.
 
• **Significance:** The 'Natyashastra' is a foundational text for classical Indian dance and theatre, influencing various art forms and cultural practices in India.
